Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-07

- Duration: 52 minutes

Auto-summary (auto): Quick qualify, infra constraints, next steps.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining; i'm alex from redwood, with priya our se. can you do quick intros?
00:12 Samir (NovaPulse, CTO): sure i'm samir, cto at novapulse, we build realtime triage assist for hosps, so PHI is a thing. ana is our head of ml, jordan handles infra and leah security.
00:25 Ana (Head ML): hi all. big thing for us is model latency for short prompts and also cost, we run mixed workloads, embeddings + chat + rerank.
00:35 Priya (Redwood SE): thanks, quick note: our dedicated product gives reserved GPU pools with warm-pool prewarm, can route requests by policy, and we support private onprem control plane if you need air gap.
00:49 Jordan Rivers (Infra Eng): when you say onprem control plane, do you mean we can run the control plane in our VPC and a separate inference plane on our k8s? or is it a full package?
01:02 Priya: good question. the private option can be packaged as a customer-managed control plane in your VPC with the inference nodes either in your cloud account or onprem—there are two deployment models. we also offer an onprem appliance if your security team needs no cloud egress.
01:18 Leah (Security): important for us: KMS integration, HSM support, audit logs, retention policies. can we get a SOC2 + KMS design doc?
01:26 Alex: yes we'll share SOC2 and a KMS/HSM integration note. i'll add that to next steps.
01:33 Samir: capacity question — our peak is spiky, like 20-30x baseline during day, we need burst without paying for full time reserve. how does warm-pool vs prewarm vs burst credit work?
01:47 Priya: two levers. reserved nodes (guaranteed capacity) plus warm-pool which keeps a number of nodes pre-initialized with KV cache and model weights. warm-pool reduces cold-start token latency. burst can be supported by temporary spot-like extra nodes or routed to hosted fallbacks. we also do prefix/KV cache so repeated sessions are faster.
02:10 Jordan Rivers: is the warm-pool maintaining KV cache per-tenant or global? privacy matters.
02:18 Priya: we support tenant-fenced warm pools—each tenant's cache is isolated on dedicated lanes if you choose strict isolation. otherwise we can do soft multi-tenant warm pools for cost efficiency. sounds like you want strict?
02:28 Samir: yes, PHI = stricter. we'd prefer fenced reservations.
02:32 Ana: what's the expected p99 latency impact for a fenced warm-pool versus shared?
02:38 Priya: fenced adds a bit of overhead in utilization, so unit-cost up a bit and effective burst headroom smaller; p99 for short prompts (less than 256 tokens) we typically see 150-350ms on A100-like hardware when warmed, 600-1000ms if cold. those numbers vary by model and sequence length.
03:03 Alex: tradeoff: cost vs deterministic latency. dedicated reserved nodes give you predictable throughput and control plane for pinning model versions. you can pair with automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant for non-PHI traffic if acceptable.
03:18 Jordan Rivers: can we do regional fallbacks? our main region is us-east-1 and we prefer no cross-region PHI routing.
03:26 Priya: yes—routing rules can be region-bound; fallbacks can be configured to only route non-sensitive traffic. KMS keys can be region-scoped too.
03:35 Ana: on the benchmarking — we want p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. can you run with our sample traces?
03:42 Priya: absolutely. if you share histograms and a sample spike window we'll run a 1h synthetic with your sequence lengths and concurrency profile. we'll include trace logs and token-level cost.
03:50 Samir: and the onprem option—what's required for network and hardware ops? we have a small onprem GPU cluster but not heavy infra ops.
03:59 Priya: onprem requires node requisites (GPUs with certain drivers), a lightweight orchestrator agent, and either a customer-managed control plane in VPC or an offline control plane if air-gapped. we can provide a runbook; if you prefer we can take managed infra as part of Dedicated with a VPC peering model.
04:18 Leah (Security): encryption — TLS in transit and encryption at rest, and can we use our own KMS key for HSM?
04:26 Alex: yes, bring-your-own-KMS supported for Private and Dedicated; HSM integrations available for enterprise. we'll attach a KMS integration note.
04:33 Jordan Rivers: curious about evictions and preemption. if we reserve nodes, can they be preempted for emergencies?
04:39 Priya: reserved nodes are non-preemptible for your pool. we also offer burst capacity that's preemptible with cheaper pricing. autoscaling policies can be tuned for failover windows so critical queries hit reserved nodes first.
04:52 Ana: any experience with throughput for reranking workloads? we do a lot of candidate scoring (512 tokens x 64 candidates) which is heavy.
05:01 Priya: we typically recommend batching for rerank workloads, and in Dedicated we can tune kernel selection and quantization to accelerate that path; we'll need to see your candidate counts and sequence length. batching strategy affects latency tradeoffs.
05:20 Alex: one thing: quantify expected steady-state and expected peak; our reserved sizing model uses a P95 concurrency target and adds warm pool buffer for spikes.
05:30 Samir: i'll be honest, we also evaluated an internal self-hosted stack and a managed cloud vendor. cost is comparable but we don't want to own the orchestration and optimization. can you outline OPEX differences?
05:44 Alex: we'll include an OPEX comparison in the spreadsheet — reserved monthly commitment vs pay-as-you-go hosted and estimate engineering time to operate self-hosted.
05:52 Jordan Rivers: SLA — do you offer uptime and latency SLAs for Dedicated?
05:57 Priya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; specifics depend on contract tier. for critical workloads we recommend Reserved + Warm-pool + 24x7 support add-on.
06:07 Leah (Security): audits and access controls — role-based access, SAML/SSO, audit logs with retention settings?
06:14 Alex: yes RBAC and SSO are supported, audit logs can be retained per customer policy; in Private you can store logs in your own bucket. we'll provide a security pack.
06:26 Ana: timeline — we want to pilot within the next 3 weeks and if benchmarks look good we may commit to a quarter of reserved capacity. possible?
06:33 Alex: feasible. pilot -> benchmark -> 1-2 week tuning -> commit. we should plan the pilot for next week; priya will run the perf harness.
06:42 Priya: i'll need a small sample dataset and a histogram of request rates. also please share SLOs: target p50/p95/p99 and cost constraints.
06:53 Samir: i'll have my team send that by thursday.
06:57 Alex: recap: we'll send pricing + reserved sizing spreadsheet, security/KMS note, and SE will run the benchmark. sync next week to review results.
07:08 Jordan Rivers: one last question — what's the rollback behavior if a new model increases latency?
07:14 Priya: rollouts can be canary and automatic fallback to previous model or to a safe hosted variant; we support percentage-based canaries and automatic rollback on latency regressions for requests flagged by evals.
07:28 Ana: nice. also can you store prompts for eval regressions? we need prompt-level repro to debug quality deltas.
07:36 Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize and the Console keep prompt sets and regression alerts; we can hook that to your eval pipeline.
07:46 Alex: ok wrapping up, thanks everyone. we'll attach docs and next steps in CRM.
07:51 Leah: thanks.
07:53 Samir: thanks all.

End of transcript.
